scope: One bounded local read-only review of new installer, health, builder, three focused test files and nonsecret owner-packet-v4; only presence verification of prior 120-second finalization/non-trading fixes. No whole reader re-audit.

findings.title: Keep the stop and executable-health integrity checks active under optimized Python
findings.trigger: An owner invokes the installer or existing health wrapper with python -O/-OO or inherited PYTHONOPTIMIZE. The new entrypoints do not reject optimized execution.
findings.defect: The otherwise explicit need-based installer calls pinned base.quiet/quiet_state, whose stopped-owner checks are Python assert statements and vanish under optimization. Its generated new-wrapper also uses assert as its only hash gate before runpy executes health.py, allowing changed health code to execute under optimization. Account flock and other guards still exist; this is a bypass of mandatory stopped-state and pre-execution code-binding checks, not evidence of a live double writer.
findings.evidence: Static inspection: base_ops.py lines 83-85 contains only assertions; handoff lines 291/352/369 call those checks without a sys.flags.optimize guard. Builder line 43 and loader line 219 require an assert-based wrapper. Current new-wrapper.py has that exact form. The 44 tests run in ordinary Python and do not exercise optimized execution.
findings.narrow_fix: Add an unconditional optimized-interpreter rejection before operational imports/reads/claims (including the SystemOps entrypoint) while reusing the accepted pinned base, or implement the few quiet-state checks with need locally. Generate and validate a wrapper with an unconditional if/hash-mismatch raise before runpy. Rebuild/rebind packet hashes and material; keep accepted reader unchanged.
findings.targeted_regression: Use only temporary fictional fixtures: python -O/PYTHONOPTIMIZE must reject an operational installer mode before SystemOps actions; a generated wrapper with modified temporary health bytes must fail before executing a marker under normal and optimized Python. If using explicit quiet-state checks, test active/deactivating/nonzero-PID and override states remain rejected.
